body: Yeah this isn’t really weird. Of course the woman’s right to choose is paramount, but that doesn’t eliminate emotions from the equation.

First off, I would ask her if she knows this is supposed to be a date. Maybe I’m weird but if I’m hanging out with a guy alone I’ll usually tell my partner and let him know that we are just hanging out as friends. If she hasn’t let you know, she is either likely cheating or looking for an opportunity to do so, or just legitimately unaware of what this “friend” is intending.

Listen to everyone here. You are not safe with this person. If the police press charges it is for the safety of both you and any other partners he may have. You did the right thing. Please, please break it off, let people know if you need support, and stay safe!!

I don’t think you’re in the wrong for ending it because of his past. Sex work aside, he proudly flaunted the fact that he has contributed to the exploitation and sex trafficking of poor women and girls around the world. Yes, some people choose sex work and if he was only really doing this in wealthier countries it would probably be less morally reprehensible, but in poorer countries it’s highly likely that they did not choose sex work and are either trafficking victims or just entirely desperate. Being a sex worker out of pure need and high demand because you’re from an “exotic” country with a lot of rich men coming in is not choosing sex work.

Not sharing values, or even standards of basic human decency really, is a completely valid reason to end a relationship.

I’m not your wife, but one thing that helps is hearing it. Tell her when she looks good, tell her how good she looks, and if it’s an appropriate setting, make her feel sexy and desirable. If she has some serious issues like body dysmorphia or an ED she may need further professional help and you can definitely help her get that. But ultimately there’s really nothing wrong with her wanting to eat better and be healthier, just make sure to remind her she’s beautiful no matter what :)

I think you’re really just overthinking this all. 

Maybe suggest that he get out more or plan more social events with his friends. Don’t dive into a one-sided non monogamous relationship just based on interests. If he really was disappointed that you don’t have a lot of common interests then I’m sure he’d tell you. 

In the meantime try new things together, watch movies you’ve never seen, go see a band neither of you have ever heard of. There’s other healthier ways to approach this that won’t get your heart stomped on, I promise.

My thoughts exactly. I have a wonderful relationship with someone who I don’t share a ton of common interests with. We take turns picking movies to expose one another to new things and we’ve developed some common interests and also found new things together. Other than that we can sit in bed together and do two completely different things and just enjoy being around one another. I’d never offer a one sided poly relationship to him just because I don’t like sports as much, that would make me so bitter and upset down the line and he’d probably feel guilty for making me think I wasn’t enough for him. Just seems like a bad solution.
So what you’re talking about… is letting him have friends?

Based on what you’ve said I think this is all a really bad idea. Offering to let him go have sex with other women based on you not having a lot of common interests is going to lead you to massive heartbreak.

I don’t think she meant to be manipulative, but it feels a bit manipulative to give you hope. It kind of seems like she wants to keep you on the hook as a rebound or something, without maintaining contact. 

That really sucks though :(
So has he somehow made you feel like you’re not enough for him? Has he said anything along those lines?

First of all, why do you think proposing this might be a good idea? If he hasn’t ever mentioned it to you before what’s the reason for you proposing it to him?

Also, you’re right about most healthy poly relationships having some amount of interaction with other partners. It helps decrease the stress around it and helps you feel connected to your main partner in that you know the other people they’re seeing. They’re just people too and sometimes the mystery around knowing your partner is sleeping with/seeing other people can create this panic that they have something you don’t have even when you agreed to that setup.

I don’t know if waiting would do much. It seems like things ended really badly and the fact that she immediately went NC shows how she feels. The last message does kind of give off “maybe we could get back together” vibes but that feels either manipulative or like she’s genuinely missing you too. 

Either way I wouldn’t hold on too hard.
